parsed.explanation: No trans-specific evidence is documented, so the rating extrapolates from structural signals: same-sex conduct is regularly prosecuted, gender identity has no anti-discrimination protection, severe stigma and taboo prevail amid civil war, impunity and statelessness, and the regime splits by control. In government areas civil law allows 3 months to 3 years' imprisonment with regular prosecutions and police surveillance. In insurgent and southern regional areas capital punishment for consensual same-sex activity is recorded as imposed, with armed-group killings documented through 2024. A visibly trans visitor in such an environment faces outing, prosecution, detention and, in death-penalty zones, lethal targeting, with no documented recourse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Regular prosecutions in government areas; prison up to three years under Article 409 and police surveillance under Article 410. Custody conditions for trans visitors not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch or police encounter could lead into the criminalised same-sex regime, but this pathway is not documented for trans visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Same-sex conduct criminalised; capital punishment under sharia interpretations in some regions and recorded as imposed in insurgent/southern areas. No gender-identity anti-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No known government executions reported in 2022; impunity remained the norm, which is not a protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality law is the documented lever; in a thin trans-specific record it is extrapolated as risk to a gender-nonconforming visitor, not treated as a dead letter.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Severe societal stigma, no public discussion, pervasive violence and statelessness. Non-state armed groups killed people alleged to have engaged in homosexual activity in 2017, 2018 and 2024.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Impunity and conflict weaken any police protection; raw killing counts have no denominator and cannot establish a per-capita trans rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No prohibition of discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity; no record of relief for trans visitors; penalty sources conflict and 2022 enforcement data absent.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of trans-specific, entry, facilities and care evidence is uncertainty, not safety, and resolves toward the documented criminal and conflict regime.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower severity certainty than 0.05-A: execution is documented for same-sex activity in insurgent/southern zones and killings occurred in 2024, but no trans-presentation execution and no government execution were documented, so a lethal pathway is credible in parts of the combined regime rather than highly likely everywhere.

Similar to 0.15-B: imprisonment, detention and capital provisions, weak recourse and state/variding control. This case is comparable or slightly lower because capital punishment is recorded as imposed in some zones, not merely authorised, while custodial abuse for trans visitors is not documented.

Materially worse than 0.35-B: consequences are not limited to hours-long stops and fines. Regular prosecution with up to three years in government areas and death in insurgent/southern areas, plus armed-group killings and severe stigma, place it well below the 0.35 detention-without-imprisonment pattern.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is geographically split: government areas impose short prison terms with regular prosecutions, while insurgent and southern administration zones expose people to capital punishment for same-sex activity. With no trans-specific protections, no anti-discrimination law, severe stigma, civil-war impunity and armed-group killings, an outed trans visitor has no documented remedy and faces imprisonment in government areas and possible death in capital zones. Unknowns on borders, facilities and care do not offset these documented exposures.
